_: People sheets for Argonians in the slice roster, one per upbringing (lane 2.5a2). Upbringings inferred from roster roles and zones; npcs.json carries no upbringing field.

norms.text: A person is named by tribe and office before their own name; a stranger is addressed by what they are.
Disputes go to the tree-minder or a chosen arbitrator; an apology plus owed work ends them.
The dead are staked into the mud with a carved grave-stake so they cannot float up or rise.
Raids between tribes are forgiven quickly; all are people of the root.

taboos.text: Boiling or distilling Hist sap; the tree feels it.
Taking a trinket from a xanmeer; the ruins are kept as warnings, not treasure.

values.text: The Hist bond, voluntary and older than any law.
Letting go of what has passed; holding on is shunatei.
Riddles, which the river-folk trade where others trade news.

contempts.text: Collaborators who sold their own: the old Archein families, whatever they now call themselves.
Outsiders who drain and plant the marsh and leave.

place.text: Home is the reach of this tribe's Hist roots; beyond them is somewhere else.

work.text: Work is seasonal and shared; the whole tribe labours in nushmeeko without pay.

people.text: Ojel are watched, fed and sent away; most cannot read body speech.

faction.text: The Wardens in the cities claim to speak for the Wild Ones without being asked.

hist.text: The tree is spoken of plainly as kin; it is never explained to an outsider.

empire.text: The Empire is a story the old ones tell about roads that rotted the cargo.

trade.text: Barter in tools, salt, sap, hide and owed labour; coin is a city thing.

danger.text: The marsh is not dangerous to those it raised; it is dangerous to everyone else.

rumour.text: News comes by the root-herald and is weighed against what the tree-minder dreamed.

directions.text: Directions are given by water, root and landmark, never by miles.

addressTerms.text: Strangers by category: ojel, warrior, traveller.
Elders by office: naheesh, tree-minder, kaal.

oaths.text: Emotional qualifiers at full strength: "I extend the claw of welcome."

neverSaid.text: What the Hist said in the last dream-wallow.

grievances.text: The state takes customs at the ports and gives the interior nothing back.
Foreign diggers still come for the xanmeers.

rumours.text: A Black-Tongue clutch has been keeping its Shadow-born hatchlings instead of sending them anywhere.

views.text: Pitied, not hated: they cannot hear the tree and it is not their fault.
City cousins, quick-mouthed and worn smooth.
A city government that names the interior its constituency.
Tree-minders talking to tree-minders; the right way to argue.

norms.text: Business with ojel is done in complete sentences and practical imperatives.
The tide and the cargo set the day, not the sun.
A city Hist is a second government; its tender is consulted before the council.

taboos.text: Calling another Argonian lukiul in public.
Praising Umbriel or those who brought it.

values.text: A berth, a boat and a share; the port lives by moving small loads fast.
Using the old names with kin and the ojel names with ojel.

contempts.text: Dock masters who hire with a debtor's Owing months.
Interior pride that has never seen a ledger.

place.text: The port is home; the interior is where family lives and visits are long.

work.text: Work is a berth bought, a cargo moved and a share split; debtors' months pay for most berths.

people.text: Ojel are customers first; you learn which ones pay.

faction.text: The Wardens hold the customs house and little else.

hist.text: The city tree is tended and feared at once.

empire.text: The Company wharves are still here; the Company is gone, good riddance.

trade.text: Small cargo, fast boats, cash at the wharf.

danger.text: Pirates on the water and debt on the land.

rumour.text: Everything comes through the docks first.

directions.text: Directions by channel, quay and ferry price.

addressTerms.text: Captain, pilot or factor, by the job.

oaths.text: "Stay moist" as a farewell, worn smooth.

grievances.text: Berths are bought with months of a debtor's work.
The coasts are unpoliced and the state has no navy.

rumours.text: A new merchant council seat is for sale at the next tariff vote.

views.text: Proud cousins who think a ledger is a curse.
Neighbours on the quay; half the port is them.
The other people of the Southern Sea trade.
The crews who make the routes work; they charge well.

norms.text: Imperial law, contracts and the courthouse are the normal way to settle a wrong.
A Tamrielic god, Dibella or Zenithar or Seth, is kept at home, quietly.
Hissmir's trials are spoken of as a pilgrimage one might make someday.

taboos.text: Saying the word lukiul about oneself.
Speaking of 4E 48 as anything but a massacre of people like us.

values.text: Citizenship and property that do not depend on a tree.
Records, filings and the written instrument.

contempts.text: Nativists who still call them assimilated.
Being pitied by those who never left.

place.text: Gideon and the mixed cities are home; the interior is a foreign country.

work.text: Work is paid in coin and written down.

people.text: Imperial neighbours are neighbours; the tribes are strangers who share a face.

faction.text: The Wardens are the heirs of the men who tried to kill us.

hist.text: The tree does not speak to us. It is easier to say so plainly.

empire.text: The Empire left a courthouse that still works, which is more than anyone else left.

trade.text: The Blackwood Road and Leyawiin keep the city fed.

danger.text: The marsh is dangerous; we know the road and we keep to it.

rumour.text: Rumour is what is said before it is filed.

directions.text: Directions by street, gate and mile.

addressTerms.text: Imperial forms: sir, madam, citizen, master.
Emotional qualifiers omitted, or one beat late.

oaths.text: By the Nine, or by Dibella, out of habit.

neverSaid.text: That they cannot hear the Hist, to a marsh-born.

grievances.text: The state that rules them was founded by the movement that tried to exterminate them.

rumours.text: The League means to petition for citizenship without a tribe again.

views.text: They pity us and expect thanks for it.
The only body that argues for us as citizens.

norms.text: An Owing worked off is over; by custom it is never mentioned again.
Bones of the dead are carried home to their Hist where they can be.

taboos.text: Naming who sold your months, in front of them.
Asking a washed-out worker how long they have been away.

values.text: Getting home to one's own tree before colour and soul fade.
An ending: a sentence that finishes.

contempts.text: Crossing-holders who add food and spoilage to the account.
Those who call it a custom when it has become a chain.

place.text: Home is a tree far from here.

work.text: The work belongs to a holder's ledger; it grows faster than it can be paid.

people.text: Other debtors are family; holders are weather.

faction.text: The state has not touched the Owing; the Chainbreakers at least burn the books.

hist.text: The ledger cannot sell the tree.

empire.text: The Imperials built the prisons and the ex-Archeins kept the ledgers.

trade.text: In trade, the debtor is the cargo.

danger.text: Dying far from the tree, where the soul cannot get home.

rumour.text: Whose ledger burned and whose was copied first.

directions.text: Directions go by work-camp, crossing and holder.

addressTerms.text: Holders by title, never by name.
Other debtors by first name only.

grievances.text: Owings are sold, extended and inherited.

rumours.text: A Gideon court threw out a transferred Owing last season.

views.text: The families who held coffles now hold ledgers.
They burn the books and carry the bones home.
Their Owing ends. Ours did not.
